ut_devil_s_castle.blurb: Devil's Castle is a high limestone peak above Albion Basin at the head of Little Cottonwood Canyon, in the Wasatch. Most of its 19 listed climbs are alpine-style multi-pitch lines, with a few trad and sport routes and one ice line mixed in. Grades cluster around 5.10 and 5.11, with a handful of easier lines and a single 5.12. The rock quality is mixed, and some climbers find it loose, so a helmet is wise. Snow can linger at the base of the routes from spring into late summer, and afternoon thunderstorms are common. It sits near 10,000 feet and is often busy in season.

ut_thunderbird_garden.blurb: Thunderbird Garden is a small bouldering area on the edge of Cedar City in southwest Utah, with solid red sandstone blocks scattered through a recreation area that is shared with a disc golf course, trails and bike riders. Nearly all of its 19 climbs are boulder problems, spread over about eleven separate boulders, plus a single trad line. Problems run from VB up to V5, but most sit in the V1 to V2 range, which suits newer boulderers. The first blocks are a couple of minutes from the lot. Sandstone is weak when damp, so give it a full day of direct sun after rain.

ut_cathedral_the_2.blurb: The Cathedral is a steep limestone cave and wall at Welcome Springs, roughly 45 minutes of driving from St. George in the far southwest corner of Utah. All 19 climbs are bolted sport routes, mostly on smooth, pocketed rock, and the grades run from 5.10 into the 5.14 range, with the bulk between 5.11 and 5.14. It is a hard-climbers crag, not a place for warm-ups. The cliff faces north and stays shaded, so fall and spring work best, and early summer can be fine if temperatures cooperate. The setting is remote and quiet, though visits have increased.

ut_eavesdown_docks.blurb: Eavesdown Docks is the largest sector at Serenity, a sport climbing zone in American Fork Canyon in the Southern Wasatch. All 19 routes are bolted, running from 5.8 to 5.11, with a fairly even spread across 5.9, 5.10 and 5.11 and a few easier lines. The walls face several ways: a short south-facing wall on one side of a gully, then an overhanging north-facing section, then taller and less steep north-facing rock. That mix gives more variety than elsewhere at Serenity, and the shady north faces help on warm days. It suits moderate climbers looking for a short walk and a range of angles.

ut_wicked_crag_the.blurb: The Wicked Crag is a steep sport crag in Mill Creek Canyon in the La Sal Mountains, a short drive from Moab. It has 19 bolted routes, nearly all of them 5.12 or 5.13, with a couple of 5.14s and only a couple of easier lines, so it rewards strong climbers. The wall includes a big overhanging wave, a nearly vertical recessed section and a large overhanging fin, giving everything from powerful roof climbing to thin face moves. The northwest-facing rock is in shade most of the day with sun arriving late. Sandstone here is fragile when wet, so avoid climbing after rain.

ut_pentapitch_area.blurb: The Pentapitch Area sits on the south side of Little Cottonwood Canyon in the Wasatch, a short hike from the road. It is mainly a trad crag with several multi-pitch crack and face lines, plus three bolted sport routes. Of the 19 climbs, most are around 5.10, with a few 5.11s and a handful of easier lines from about 5.6 to 5.9. The wall faces northwest, which makes it a decent pick for hot mornings. Its signature route is a five-pitch 5.8 that draws a lot of attention, so expect company on good days.

ut_lizard_head_wall.blurb: Lizard Head Wall is a south-facing wall in Little Cottonwood Canyon, tucked between Altered States Gully and The Fin in the Wasatch. It holds 19 climbs, almost all trad, plus one bolted line. Grades start near 5.5 and mostly land between 5.9 and 5.10, with a few 5.11s. There are only a few routes, but they include some good crack lines and a pleasant slab, and the wall tends to be quiet, so solitude is likely. The approach goes up a gully and traverses west to the base, which makes it more of a scramble than a roadside crag.

ut_aqueduct_area_the.blurb: The Aqueduct Area is a small quartzite crag in Big Cottonwood Canyon, just below the Dogwood area, with a walk of roughly ten minutes. Its 19 climbs are mostly trad, with a few bolted sport routes, one top rope and one boulder problem. Grades range from about 5.6 to 5.11, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11. Anchors are bolted, so cleaning and lowering are straightforward. The rock has two faces, facing southeast and southwest, so it catches plenty of sun. Quartzite tends to feel slippery, so expect technical movement rather than big holds.
